title: Fixed state-score errors required a 1.37-species interaction for 80 percent four-sample detection in US bird designs
abstract: We tested the sensitivity of a published four-sample ozone by warmth replication rule. We rebuilt state influence scores from US bird richness designs for the East and West in 1995-2009 and 2010-2024. Under fixed score magnitudes, symmetric state signs and fixed published standard errors, a common negative interaction of 0.5 recorded species per 10 ppb ozone and 2 C warmth passed all four corrected tests in 0.153 percent of draws. An 80 percent chance required a magnitude of 1.368 species. The later western sample supplied most of this limit. Separate cell signs and independent normal errors gave similar thresholds. Exact western sign enumeration, an analytic normal check and independent score reconstruction supported the calculations. This is a conditional design diagnostic, not population power or an ecological effect estimate. Estimated errors, cross-state dependence, selected surveys, coarse exposure and detection bias limit its use. Aggregate evidence and code permit offline reproduction.

display.caption: Detection probability under fixed error references for four US bird richness designs in 1995-2024. These are conditional reference probabilities, not population power.
